title: Choosing a Container
summary: Matching the data structure to the job - the costs of the standard containers side by side, ordered versus unordered maps and sets, sorted vectors and flat maps, multisets and multimaps, problems solved by the right container (counting, grouping, first-unique, longest consecutive run), and a checklist for choosing.

cards.q: You must repeatedly find the first appointment after a given time. Which container fits?
cards.a:
std::map, using lower_bound

Hash tables cannot answer "next bigger"; ordered containers (or a sorted vector) can, in O(log n).

cards.q: A dictionary of 200,000 words is loaded once and then checked millions of times. Which is a strong choice?
cards.a:
A sorted std::vector with binary search, or a hash set

The data does not change, so a contiguous sorted vector or a hash set gives fast lookups.

cards.q: Why does the longest-consecutive-run algorithm only start counting at x when x - 1 is absent?
cards.a:
So each run is counted once, from its start

Counting from every element would recount long runs again and again, giving O(n²); starting only at run starts keeps the total work O(n).
